prompt: One continuous locked-off eye-level documentary interview shot in landscape. Invent an original fictional astronomy presenter, Professor Rowan Ellery, PhD in Physics. A white man about 49 with a broad square face, strong nose, grey-green eyes, freckles, a full neatly trimmed copper beard silvering at the chin and thick brushed-back auburn hair with silver temples. No glasses. Deep plum brushed-cotton overshirt over an oatmeal crew-neck tee. He sits upright in his own quiet study, framed from mid chest up, small breathing room above his head, looking directly into the lens. Behind him: a lived-in wall of warm walnut bookshelves with worn astronomy books, a small brass celestial globe on the left, a shaded reading lamp on the right, muted indigo wall in the recess. Soft side daylight, realistic skin texture, subtle depth of field, understated editorial portrait, no titles or visible writing. Hands below frame. Begin with about three quarters of a second of silent relaxed eye contact, lips gently closed. In a warm, resonant mid-low English-speaking voice, measured and curious, with natural articulation, say exactly: "I'm Professor Rowan Ellery. Welcome to Mysteries of the Sky. Even a hidden planet can leave a trace in starlight." Finish with relaxed eye contact, gently closed lips. Subtle natural blinks, one small nod, no cuts, no push-in, no music, just clean close-mic speech and faint room tone. Keep the face, camera, wardrobe and room consistent throughout.
